ut_ashley_creek_bouldering.blurb: A small bouldering zone in the hills north of Vernal, with eleven problems scattered over a dirt hillside that faces north, tucked beneath a short band of rock and just east of the creek. The boulders are sandstone, mostly clean though a few feel grainy, and the area stretches roughly a mile by half a mile. Problems run from VB-level up to about V4, with the bulk of them in the V0 to V3 range, so it suits newer boulderers and anyone wanting a quiet, low-key session. Landings can turn muddy in spring after a wet winter.

ut_cragganmore.blurb: Cragganmore is a steep, tall wall in Maple Canyon's Right Fork, built around a big overhanging cave with a capping roof. All eleven routes are bolted sport lines, and they lean hard toward the top end: one in the low 5.10s, a couple of 5.11s, and most of the rest around 5.12. Lines run longer and more overhung than those at the neighbouring Minimum Wall, so expect sustained endurance climbing on cobbles. The cave keeps most routes shaded and dry in light rain, which makes it a handy fallback when the weather turns.

ut_red_slab.blurb: Red Slab is the first rock you meet when heading up Rock Canyon above Provo, a short west-facing slab of quartzite with a quick walk from the canyon mouth. Eleven routes, mostly bolted sport lines plus a few trad, spread from about 5.5 up to 5.10, with the easy and moderate grades making up the bulk. Short, friendly and popular, it is a good place for new leaders to get comfortable on the sharp end, and the classic namesake line makes a natural first lead. Expect company on weekends.

ut_lonely_challenge_area.blurb: Lonely Challenge Area sits high on the slope above Stairs Gulch in Big Cottonwood Canyon, on a tall, smooth expanse of dark quartzite that faces east. Eleven routes, mainly trad with three sport lines, range from about 5.7 to 5.12, with the heaviest cluster around 5.10. The wall offers some gentler warm-ups, a few long bolted lines and several harder test pieces, and it is a quieter alternative to the busier Challenge Buttress nearby. A tight gully holds shade through the afternoon, and the scramble up talus to the base takes roughly twenty minutes.

ut_private_pizza_wall.blurb: Private Pizza Wall is a roadside crag in Lower Buckhorn Wash, in the San Rafael Swell, climbing solid Wingate sandstone. Of its eleven routes, nine are trad, with one sport line and one aid line, and the free climbs span roughly 5.7 to 5.10. Most lines run about sixty to eighty feet, so it works well for a day of relaxed cragging with a standard rack. The namesake crack and dihedral route is the long-time classic of the wall, and newer additions have since filled in the rest of the face.
